title: chat-v1 param negotiator, stream-heartbeat, and function-call retry stabilization
author: Aisha Khan
description: Context and motivation: Customers using the OpenAI /v1/chat.completions compatibility layer reported a few classes of intermittent production issues: (1) parameter mismatches when callers provide overlapping or deprecated fields (max_tokens vs max_output_tokens, temperature vs temp), causing surprising truncation or runaway outputs; (2) streaming instability on long-lived connections where intermediate frames are dropped and clients deadlock; (3) function/tool-calling sessions that mis-handle transient tool errors during the handshake resulting in unhelpful 5xxs; and (4) inconsistent stop/logprobs envelopes when role aliases or stop-priority lists are present. This PR introduces a cohesive "param negotiator" to normalize and coalesce incoming v1 parameters, a lightweight stream-heartbeat/frame-resequencer to reduce client-observed stalls, and a retry-safe function-call handshake with stricter structured-output envelopes. Summary of changes: 1) Param negotiator: new mapping layer that merges and validates common OpenAI fields (max_tokens -> max_output_tokens, top_p clamping, temperature aliases). It implements precedence rules, warns to logs (structured event) when deprecated fields are used, and exposes a feature-flag to toggle conservative vs permissive merging. 2) Role aliasing table: supports mapping common role synonyms (assistant/bot/system-helper) and preserves original role metadata for downstream evals. 3) Stop sequence priority: normalize and dedupe stop sequences, and convert mixed-type stop specs (string | array) into deterministic priority lists so logprobs and stop-detection are consistent. 4) Logprob envelope normalization: emit a compact logprobs section even for streaming partials to maintain downstream scorer compatibility. 5) Stream heartbeat and resequencer: periodic small ping frames inserted for idle streams, plus a resequencer that tolerates out-of-order fragments from transport retries; defaults tuned to 8s heartbeat and 2x resequence window. 6) Function-call handshake retry/backoff: retry on transient tool initialization errors (HTTP 502/503) with an idempotent handshake token; on persistent failure falls back to a capped text-only response and emits an audit event. 7) Structured-output mode: new "record" framing that encloses tool outputs with a stable JSON envelope and schema hints for consumer SDKs. 8) Docs, SDK compatibility shims, and extensive unit + integration tests. Backwards compatibility and migration: default behavior preserves existing responses unless the customer flips the "param-negotiator.conservative=false" runtime flag. The role aliasing and stop normalization are backward compatible (they only change tie-breakers for ambiguous inputs). Tests and QA: added integration harness scenarios that replay production traces for 7 distinct failure modes (stream disconnect, tool handshake flaps, mixed stop types). Checklist: - [x] Implement negotiator and tests - [x] Add stream heartbeat + resequencer - [x] Add function-call retry + audit events - [x] Add structured-output envelope and SDK doc notes - [x] Add integration traces and unit tests - [x] Run CI and address flaky tests Notes: This is deliberately conservative in the default rollout; feature flags allow canarying across Dedicated and Private clusters. Related: ENG-2147 (param negotiation), ENG-2201 (stream stability), SUP-4821 (customer incident that prompted auto-retries).

ci_summary: CI passed on rerun. One flaky network test (tests/e2e/connectivity) failed on first run, rerun passed. All new unit and integration tests are green across linux/amd64 and linux/arm64 lanes.
release_notes: Improved OpenAI /v1/chat.completions parity: added a param negotiator that normalizes deprecated/overlapping parameters, stream-heartbeat with resequencing to reduce client stalls, retry-safe function-call handshake with graceful fallback, canonical stop/logprob normalization, and a structured 'record' output envelope for tool outputs. Rollout behind feature flags for controlled canaries.
